meta.title: AI grading — golden set
meta.subtitle: How the AI grades real handwritten work — and how it shows its math
meta.framing: Illustrative seeded demo data, not a real student. The 73% receipt below is one worked example, captured live from the product so you can read the mechanism — Veradic grades real photographed work this exact way; the names and numbers here are there to show how.

hero.headline: Hand it a photo. Get the whole class graded — every point explained — before your coffee's cold.
hero.subhead: Grading nights at the kitchen table. The quiet worry of whether a 73 is actually fair — or whether the same paper would've earned a 78 on a different evening. Veradic reads each student's handwritten work, grades every problem, and shows you exactly where each point went. You review the few it's unsure about, then sign off.

flowSetup.title: The work comes in already graded
flowSetup.caption: Open Submissions to a class that's already scored — five ready to review, not thirty to grade from a blank rubric. You're reviewing, not starting over.

flowSetup.title: The work and the read, side by side
flowSetup.caption: The student's actual photographed page sits right beside the AI's grade and its reasoning — one screen, nothing to cross-reference, every problem in reach.

moment.eyebrow: The moment that sets it apart
moment.title: Every point, accounted for.
moment.body: Most tools hand back a number and leave you to trust it. Veradic shows the receipt. Full credit for the setup. Full credit for the method. Then each place a point came off, named in plain words and sized — a −20% sign error, a −7% arithmetic slip — adding up to a score you can read straight down the page.
moment.sell: 100 − 20 (sign error) − 7 (arithmetic) = 73 — no black-box score; a breakdown you and the student can both see.
moment.note: Illustrative seeded example — Maya Chen isn't a real student. The receipt is captured live from the product so you can read exactly how a grade is built.

flowResolution.title: Each deduction points to the exact step
flowResolution.caption: The −20% sign error highlights step 3 of the handwriting; the −7% arithmetic slip highlights step 5. The grade is tied to the work itself, not floating above it — so you can check the read in seconds.

flowResolution.title: Your time goes only where the AI was unsure
flowResolution.caption: The roster sorts itself — one student needs your eyes, five the AI is confident on. A low-confidence read is surfaced, not buried, so your attention lands on the one paper that needs it.

flowResolution.title: You're the judge — one click to override
flowResolution.caption: Disagree with the AI's Partial 73%? Tap Full. It records that you overrode the suggestion and keeps a one-tap revert. The AI proposes; the teacher decides — every time.

flowResolution.title: Nothing reaches a student until you say so
flowResolution.caption: Grades stay private until you publish. The confirm step tells you exactly what's going out — how many you reviewed, how many are still AI-suggested — so nothing slips out by accident.

payoff.title: What a teacher gets back.
payoff.lead: Not another inbox to babysit. Four things that change how grading feels:

points.title: Graded in minutes, not nights
points.body: The class comes in already scored. You review the handful the AI flagged instead of carrying the whole stack home to the kitchen table.

points.title: Every grade you can defend
points.body: When a parent asks why it's a 73, you have the receipt: full credit for the setup, a −20 sign error in step 3, a −7 arithmetic slip in step 5. Not an opinion — a breakdown.

points.title: Consistent across the whole class
points.body: The same rubric, applied the same way to every paper. The student in period 3 is graded by the same standard as the one in period 1 — no drift as the night wears on.

points.title: You stay in control
points.body: Nothing is final until you publish, every score is one tap to override, and the student never sees a grade you didn't sign off on.

payoff.closing: Graded in minutes, every point explained, the same standard for every kid — and you still sign off on each one. That's the whole point.
